output.interpretation: Two-group comparison: patient-derived pancreatic cancer organoids (mostly PDAC PDOs grown in Matrigel/3D culture) treated in vitro with a drug (case) versus the same PDO lines given vehicle (DMSO/medium) or left untreated (control). Doses and time points can be pooled. This should be done within one series, using human bulk RNA-seq with NCBI-generated raw counts and at least 3 samples per arm. Ideally each organoid line should have both a treated and an untreated sample, so the analysis can be paired by line.

clarifying_questions.question: Which drug or drug class do you mean? 'A drug' could match many separate GEO series, each testing a different compound, and pooling them would mix unrelated biology.
options: FOLFIRINOX or its parts (5-FU, irinotecan/SN-38, oxaliplatin)
KRAS inhibitors (e.g. MRTX1133 for G12D, sotorasib/adagrasib for G12C, pan-RAS such as RMC-6236)
Any drug, analysed one series at a time
clarifying_questions.why: This decides which series qualify. Each series usually tests one or a few compounds. Without a drug, more than 10 series could qualify, and they would not answer the same question.

clarifying_questions.question: What counts as the untreated control?
options: Vehicle or plain medium (untreated) are both fine
clarifying_questions.why: Some PDO series use only vehicle controls and others use medium-only controls. This changes which samples go in the control arm.

clarifying_questions.question: Should the organoids come only from primary PDAC tissue (surgical resection or EUS-FNA biopsy), or are these also acceptable: PDX-derived organoids, organoids from metastases or ascites, organoids grown with fibroblasts or immune cells, and other pancreatic tumour types (e.g. neuroendocrine)?
clarifying_questions.why: These are not interchangeable models. PDX-derived organoids, co-cultures and neuroendocrine organoids would each be a different sample set. The answer also determines whether mouse KPC organoid series (to be excluded) look relevant.

clarifying_questions.question: If one series includes several doses or time points, should all treated samples be pooled into one case arm, or should you pick one dose/time (e.g. the longest exposure or the IC50 dose)?
options: Pool all doses and time points
Use one dose/time point per series
clarifying_questions.why: Your question allows any dose or time, but pooling early and late time points weakens or confuses the signal. This changes which GSMs go in the case arm.
